title: The Book of Nature Open Lies
description: The Book of Nature Open Lies in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 81, “The book of creation”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The book of na-ture o-pen lies, With much in-struc-tion stored; But till the Lord a-noints our eyes We can-not read a word.

lines: The book of nature open lies,
But till the Lord anoints our eyes
And guessed, from age to age;
For reason's eye could ne'er attain
Though to each star they give a name,
The truths which all the stars proclaim,
With skill to measure earth and sea;
The knowledge of the saints excels
To them his secrets God reveals,
To them the sun and stars on high,
The flow'rs that paint the field,
And all the artless birds that fly,
The creatures on their senses press,
Thus may we study nature's book
And pity those who only look

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
